title: External SIGKILL composite checkpoint crash consistency
supported_claim: On the tested same-host Ubuntu/POSIX GitHub runner with SQLite, a distinct child writer process was externally terminated by its parent with SIGKILL after explicit stage markers emitted only after the corresponding durable SQLite commits. Across the preregistered before-insert, durable-PENDING, authenticated-PENDING, and durable-CURRENT kill boundaries, fresh-process reopening did not create false CURRENT state, stale-state recovery was denied after permit-ledger, reconciliation-ledger, or authority-epoch drift, exact matching authenticated PENDING state could be reconciled exactly once, post-CURRENT response-loss replay returned the same durable checkpoint, semantic issuance rebinding and predecessor/authentication tampering failed closed, trusted-minimum rollback/deletion checks held, same-generation child-writer races produced at most one CURRENT checkpoint, and clean higher-generation issuance remained live.
important_scope_limit: The Pilot 9 worker is a separate process for abrupt-death durability testing, but it is not an isolated checkpoint-signing authority: the composite HMAC key is supplied to the child by the parent harness, and the parent/test environment also possesses that key.
not_proven: Physical power-loss semantics or storage-device cache durability
Arbitrary operating-system, kernel, filesystem, or hardware failures beyond the tested SIGKILL and SQLite behavior
Separate-process isolation of the checkpoint signing key from the caller
Atomic commitment across independent storage systems
Atomic commitment to an external KMS, HSM, or checkpoint service
Protection after compromise of both SQLite state and the composite key or trusted-minimum authority
next_falsification_target: EXP-I Pilot 10: process-isolated composite checkpoint authority. Move checkpoint minting/verification authority and its key into a distinct child authority process with its own durable monotonic store, ensure the caller path possesses no checkpoint signing key, and test issuance, verification, replay, same-generation conflict refusal, restart monotonicity, stale verification, authority unavailability, and positive liveness without granting model/reviewer/production/release authority.
